label: EU(7)-PIM: anticholinergic antiparkinson medicines
title: Anticholinergic antiparkinson medicine in an older person
statement: Trihexyphenidyl | In lists: 1, 5 (A); 2, 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of anticholinergic and CNS side effects including orthostatic hypotension, falls, sedation, weakness, confusion, amnesia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Start low–go slow. M | Alternatives: Levodopa; carbidopa-levodopa; benserazide levodopa; irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase as rasagiline. E || Biperiden | In lists: 1, 3 (A); 2, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of anticholinergic and CNS side effects including orthostatic hypotension, falls, sedation, weakness, confusion, amnesia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Levodopa; carbidopa-levodopa; benserazide levodopa; irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase as rasagiline. E || Tropatepin | In lists: 1 (A); 2, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of anticholinergic and CNS side effects including orthostatic hypotension, falls, sedation, weakness, confusion, amnesia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Levodopa; carbidopa-levodopa; benserazide levodopa; irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase as rasagiline. E || Benzatropine | In lists: 2, 6 (B) | Main reason: Risk of anticholinergic and CNS side effects including orthostatic hypotension, falls, sedation, weakness, confusion, amnesia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Start low–go slow. M | Alternatives: Levodopa; carbidopa-levodopa; benserazide levodopa; irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase as rasagiline. E

plain_summary: Benzhexol, benzatropine and similar medicines can cause confusion, falls, dizziness on standing and sedation in older people.

medicine_groups.name: Anticholinergic antiparkinson medicines
medicine_groups.note: Trihexyphenidyl was previously called benzhexol. Benzatropine may also appear as benztropine. Each pair refers to one medicine. Akineton tablets count as biperiden. Benzatropine tablets and injections count.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or older has at least one supply of any Group A medicine (benzhexol or trihexyphenidyl, biperiden, tropatepine or benzatropine). Any strength counts. If age is missing and any Group A medicine is supplied, report only a possible finding and ask whether the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: Why the medicine was prescribed (Parkinson's disease or side effects of an antipsychotic), whether it is working, and any confusion, falls or dizziness on standing.
ask_the_gp: Whether the anticholinergic medicine is still needed, and whether a safer option for this person is worth discussing.
